root_idea.summary: The root centers on shining or flashing, with a second branch describing the combination of black and white or other contrasting colors.
root_idea.development: From the basic idea of gleaming come lightning, brilliance, shining objects, and related figurative uses. The color branch extends to variegated ropes, animals, eyes, mountains, and terrain; other derivatives develop specialized senses from these two orientations.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb with a distinct eye- and fright-related usage.

senses.definition: To become dazzled or confounded with fright, especially of the eye or sight, which becomes fixed, wide open, or unable to see clearly.
senses.usage_conditions: Quran 75:7 uses the verb of the eye in a frightening scene. A variant reading of the same verse is explained as the eye shining or gleaming from the intensity of its fixed stare.

senses.definition: Lightning: the flash or luminous gleam associated with clouds.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic noun denotes lightning in descriptions of storm clouds, fear, and divine signs. In the expression برق الخلب, the lightning is specifically without rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shine, gleam, or glisten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a thing, a weapon, the dawn, and other objects that give off or reflect a visible gleam.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cloud or the sky, to flash or lighten; of lightning, to appear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A weather-related use describing the production or appearance of lightning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To threaten or menace, especially with evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use, often paired with رَعَدَ or expressed in the construction بَرَقَ وَرَعَدَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beautify, adorn, or display oneself; to show one's beauty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use, including the construction of presenting or displaying oneself to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a star or asterism, to rise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in time-expressions referring to how long a star remains rising in the sky.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to raise or move its tail deceptively as if pregnant when she is not.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of false signs of pregnancy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be frightened, astonished, or confounded, becoming perplexed and unable to see the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person overwhelmed by fear or astonishment; this is distinct from the eye-specific Quranic sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak or impaired, especially of sight; the same verb may describe the weakening of the feet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical weakening use distinct from temporary dazzlement or fright.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a skin or leather container, to be damaged by heat so that its butter or contents melt and separate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of heat damage to a skin or container and its contents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To add a small quantity of oil, clarified butter, or grease to food or water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The addition is specifically slight, enough to make the food or liquid somewhat greasy or glistening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of sheep, goats, or camels, to suffer abdominal illness from eating the plant بَرْوَق.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A livestock-related use referring to a complaint in the belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make the eyes glisten or to open them wide and look sharply or intently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II intensifies or causes the eye-related action; the construction may describe fixed, hard looking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To decorate or adorn a place of residence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or intensive use applied to a dwelling or place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a baseless sign, false display, or empty promise, and to accomplish little.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic reproach for something presented without reality or verification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel or journey far.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To persist or persevere in acts of disobedience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with في المعاصي.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become unattainable or impracticable for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an affair or undertaking that proves impossible to accomplish.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a sign with a sword by waving it so that it flashes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV use involving a visible signal made with a shining weapon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn or direct one's course toward lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A directional use with lightning as the destination or point of orientation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter a tract in which there is lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized motion or location construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To see lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of observers witnessing lightning, including seasonal or rain-associated lightning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be struck, assailed, or affected by lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-result use describing the effect of lightning on a person or thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be made perplexed or confounded by fright.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is overwhelmed by fear and loses the ability to find the right way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rouse or start game for hunting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized hunting usage, reported as an additional sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a place or the horizon, to shine or gleam with lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X verb describing a landscape or horizon illuminated by lightning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lightning that occurs without rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the conventional expression برق الخلب or برق خلب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lizards of the species ضَبّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural lexical item, with a proposed derivation from بَرُوقٌ or أَبْرَقُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lamb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized word, with حَمَلٌ given as its synonym.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single flash of lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine noun functions as a noun of one occurrence or flash.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fit of confusion or perplexity in which one cannot see the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a state of mental bewilderment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quantity or mass of lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A related measure-like noun used in explanations of a display of lightning; its headword is kept distinct from the Quranic noun بَرْق.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rugged or variegated ground composed of mixed stones, sand, and earth, often with contrasting colors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may designate a portion of such terrain or a broader tract when pluralized.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small amount of grease or gravy in food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized culinary use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shining strongly or conspicuously in the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied particularly to a person described as having a visibly radiant appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Variegated locusts, especially locusts marked with yellow, white, black, or other contrasting streaks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun with a singular form in ـة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The plum or a small plum-like fruit; in some usage, the apricot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A post-classical or Arabicized fruit name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The named mount associated with the Prophet's night ascent, described as a bright, swift beast between a mule and a donkey in size.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained through its brightness or speed, by comparison with lightning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that raises or moves her tail deceptively as if pregnant when she is not.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may also be applied to a scorpion because of its raised tail.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fearful, timid, or cowardly man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived personal description, distinct from the camel term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A weak, juicy plant that greens when clouds appear and may be used as emergency food in drought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two cited spellings are treated as variant names of the plant; the plant is also proverbial for gratitude to scant moisture and weakness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shining, gleaming, glistening, luster, or brilliance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of the visible quality or effect of shining.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food, milk, condiment, or water containing a small amount of grease, clarified butter, or olive oil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer either to the prepared food or to the grease added to it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely shining, brilliant, or splendid; by extension, strikingly beautiful or radiant in appearance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to bright features such as teeth and to a person characterized by beauty or brilliance; some usage includes intentional display of beauty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shining, gleaming, or glistening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective of visible brilliance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloud containing, emitting, or accompanied by lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an adjective with سحاب or سحابة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shining sword or weapon; by extension, the gleam of weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is used for swords and other weapons, including in the idiom placing paradise beneath swords.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mineral or chemical substance put into dough or flour to make it swell, including forms identified with borax, natron, or related substances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term covers several kinds distinguished by origin and properties, including substances used in polishing or medicinal preparations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man in whom one cannot trust or confide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative personal noun, with بَوَارِقُ as its plural.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of بُورَق or بَوْرَق.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nisbah-derived occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having black and white, or other strongly contrasting colors, intermixed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to ropes, mountains, animals, eyes, meadows, and similar things when contrasting colors are combined; the feminine form is used where required by agreement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized animal name distinct from the color adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name applied to locusts or crickets of the type called جَنَادِب.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural or collective animal name distinct from the lizard noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A Persian medicine reputed to be beneficial for memory.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized medicinal noun reported as a separate lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ewer or pitcher with a spout and handle, used for pouring water or other liquids.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is an Arabicized loanword; its plural is أَبَارِيقُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A highly shining sword; in some usage, a sword or bow with gleaming or variegated markings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized weapon sense distinct from the vessel noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman beautiful and splendid or brilliant in complexion; according to another usage, one who displays her beauty intentionally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of brilliance to personal appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick silk brocade or closely woven silk cloth, especially cloth interwoven with gold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized textile term with several reported explanations of its foreign origin and exact material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shining or gleaming, or the time of shining; especially the time when dawn shines.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of time or occasion, as in عند مبرق الصبح.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Quran-related eye usage and variant reading.
Reported as an additional hunting usage.
Same heat-damaged skin meaning already represented from the primary Form I entry.
Illustrative bright-teeth example covered by the broader brilliance meaning.
Beauty-related application covered by the broader brilliance meaning.
Variant plant name grouped with the closely related بَروَق entry.
Eye coloration is an explicit application of the contrasting-color adjective.
A two-colored meadow is an explicit application of the same adjective.

cautions: The verb in Quran 75:7 has a reported variant reading with a different vocalization and nuance; the displayed Quran form follows the authoritative QAC identification بَرِقَ.

Lane cites Quran passages for some distinct Arabicized or differently headed words, including إِبْرِيقٌ and إِسْتَبْرَقٌ. These are retained as their own Classical Arabic lexical entries because no corresponding QAC form group for those headwords is supplied.
